tools.name: User Personas
tools.description: Develop detailed user personas to understand your target audience's needs, motivations, behaviors, and pain points. Personas help ensure user-centered design and decision-making throughout the project lifecycle.
prompt_list: Generate three distinct user personas for a new mobile banking application, including their tech-savviness, financial goals, and frustrations with current banking solutions.
Create a primary user persona for an e-learning platform targeting working professionals seeking to upskill. Focus on their learning habits, time constraints, and career aspirations.
Develop a set of proto-personas based on initial market research for a sustainable fashion brand. Include demographics, shopping habits, and values related to sustainability.

before: Ensure persona creation is based on actual research, not stereotypes, to avoid bias.
Represent diverse user groups and avoid creating exclusionary personas.
Clearly state the research and data sources used for persona development.
after: Regularly review and update personas as new user data becomes available.
Use personas to advocate for user needs, not to justify pre-existing assumptions.

tools.name: User Research
tools.description: Plan, conduct, and synthesize user research to uncover deep insights into user behaviors, needs, and contexts. This foundational research informs product strategy and design direction.
prompt_list: Outline a user research plan to investigate how small business owners manage their social media presence. Include research questions, methodologies (e.g., interviews, surveys), and participant criteria.
Generate a set of 10 open-ended interview questions for understanding user experiences with online grocery shopping services.
Synthesize findings from a series of user interviews and create an affinity diagram to identify key themes and pain points related to project management software.

before: Obtain informed consent from all research participants, clearly explaining the purpose of the research and how their data will be used.
Ensure anonymity and confidentiality of participant data.
Compensate participants fairly for their time and effort.
after: Store research data securely and dispose of it responsibly after the project.
Report findings accurately and avoid misrepresenting data to support a particular viewpoint.

tools.name: Data Explorer
tools.description: Interactively explore and visualize complex datasets to uncover patterns, trends, and actionable insights. Transform raw data into understandable narratives that drive informed decisions.
prompt_list: Visualize sales data over the past five years, highlighting regional performance and product category trends using a combination of bar charts and line graphs.
Analyze user engagement metrics for a web application (e.g., daily active users, session duration, feature adoption) and create a dashboard to monitor key performance indicators.
Explore customer feedback data from surveys and support tickets, identifying common issues and sentiment trends using text analysis and thematic mapping.

before: Ensure data sources are reliable and the data is cleaned and preprocessed appropriately to avoid misleading visualizations.
Protect sensitive information and comply with data privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) when handling user data.
Choose visualization types that accurately represent the data and avoid distortion.
after: Clearly label all visualizations and provide context to prevent misinterpretation.
Acknowledge limitations of the data and potential biases in the analysis and interpretation.

tools.name: Content Generator
tools.description: Generate high-quality, engaging written content for various platforms based on specified topics, keywords, and target audiences. Streamline content creation for marketing, communication, and documentation.
prompt_list: Write a 500-word blog post about the benefits of remote work for employee well-being, targeting HR professionals. Include statistics and a call to action.
Generate three variations of social media posts (Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram) announcing a new product feature for a SaaS application.
Draft an email newsletter introducing a seasonal promotion for an e-commerce store, focusing on creating a sense of urgency and highlighting key products.

before: Clearly disclose when content is AI-generated, especially in contexts where transparency is crucial (e.g., news, academic writing).
Ensure generated content is original and does not plagiarize existing work. Use plagiarism checkers if necessary.
Verify the accuracy of any factual claims or data presented in the generated content.
after: Thoroughly review, edit, and humanize AI-generated content to ensure quality, tone, and alignment with brand voice.
Be mindful of potential biases in the AI model that might be reflected in the generated content and correct them.

tools.name: Prototype Builder
tools.description: Quickly create interactive prototypes to visualize and test design concepts. Ideal for iterating on user flows and gathering early feedback before development.
prompt_list: Generate an interactive prototype for a 3-step user onboarding flow for a new mobile app.
Create a clickable wireframe for the checkout process of an e-commerce website, including cart review, shipping, and payment pages.
Develop a low-fidelity prototype to test the navigation structure of a redesigned company intranet.

before: Clearly communicate that prototypes are not final products and are for testing/feedback purposes.
Focus on testing core functionality and user flows rather than visual perfection in early stages.
Ensure placeholder content is appropriate and does not misrepresent the final product's intent.
after: Document feedback gathered during prototype testing thoroughly.
Iterate on designs based on feedback before committing to full development.

tools.name: A/B Test Designer
tools.description: Design and configure A/B tests to compare different versions of a feature or design, enabling data-driven decisions for optimization and improvement.
prompt_list: Set up an A/B test to compare two different call-to-action button texts on a landing page. Define success metrics (e.g., conversion rate).
Design an experiment to test a new homepage layout against the current one, focusing on user engagement and bounce rate.
Create variations for an email subject line A/B test to optimize open rates for a marketing campaign.

before: Ensure test variations do not create significantly negative user experiences or introduce dark patterns.
Define a clear hypothesis and success metrics before starting the test.
Determine appropriate sample size and test duration to achieve statistically significant results.
after: Analyze results objectively and avoid confirmation bias.
Share learnings from both successful and unsuccessful variations with the team.

tools.name: Accessibility Checker
tools.description: Analyze designs and code for compliance with accessibility standards (WCAG), ensuring products are usable by people with a wide range of disabilities.
prompt_list: Scan a webpage URL and generate a report of WCAG 2.1 AA violations, with suggestions for fixes.
Evaluate a design mockup (e.g., Figma link) for color contrast issues and interactive element accessibility.
Check a code snippet for proper ARIA attributes and keyboard navigation support.

before: Understand that automated checkers are a tool, not a replacement for manual testing and user feedback from people with disabilities.
Prioritize fixing critical accessibility issues that create major barriers for users.
after: Integrate accessibility checks throughout the design and development process, not just at the end.
Continuously educate the team on accessibility best practices.
